55101.whatItMeans: Five-star hotels — the top tier of Indonesian hotel classification. Full-service luxury accommodation with daily or weekly stays in a dedicated building. Think Four Seasons, Ritz-Carlton, Bulgari-level operations. Rooms, suites, restaurants, pools, spas, concierge — the works.
55101.whatYouNeed:
**Small / Medium / Large**: Two licensing tiers exist.
- **Medium-Low risk path**: NIB + Standard Certificate, issued **automatically**. Self-Assessment document required covering facilities, organization, HR, and products/services. Health Feasibility Certificate needed.
- **Medium-High risk path** (higher tier): NIB + Standard Certificate within **14 working days**. Requires Self-Assessment plus LSPr-certified tourism business standard.

**Micro + Small + Medium**: Separate Medium-Low entry with periodic reporting and health cert.

**PMA:** Fully open — 100% foreign ownership.
55101.whatChanged: In KBLI 2020, ALL star-rated hotels were under a single code: 55110. In 2025, that one code was split into 55101 (5-star), 55102 (4-star), 55103 (3-star), 55104 (2-star), and 55105 (1-star). Your licensing data still comes from the old 55110 PP28 entry, but your KBLI code is now specific to your star rating. This is a CODICE_RINUMERATO — renumbered, not restructured.
55101.baliContext: Bali has some of the world's most famous five-star properties. Nusa Dua is the traditional luxury hotel corridor. Uluwatu and Ubud have attracted the newest luxury builds. If you're entering this space, know that Bali's hotel classification is enforced by the Tourism Ministry and star ratings require physical inspections. The investment threshold for a five-star hotel is massive — we're talking tens of millions of dollars minimum. Foreign investors typically structure through a PT PMA. Land acquisition in Bali is complex: foreigners can't own freehold land, so you'll use Hak Pakai (right to use) or Hak Guna Bangunan (building rights) structures.

- 56301 — Hotel bar

55104.whatItMeans: Two-Star Hotels — commercial accommodation businesses that rent out furnished rooms or suites on a short-term basis. This classification covers entire or partial buildings equipped with dedicated front desk customer service, daily housekeeping, and food/beverage services. It strictly applies to standardized hotel operations and excludes standard residential villas or unclassified homestays.
55104.whatYouNeed:
PP28 data inherited from parent code 55110. Three distinct licensing tiers exist:

**Tier 1 — Kecil/Menengah/Besar**: Medium-Low risk (Menengah Rendah). NIB + Standard Certificate issued **automatically** (Otomatis). Self-Assessment document covering Hotel Star standards (Sarana, Organisasi, SDM, Pelayanan, Produk, Manajemen). Health Feasibility Certificate required. Authority: Bupati/Walikota.

**Tier 2 — Kecil/Menengah/Besar**: Medium-High risk (Menengah Tinggi). NIB + Standard Certificate within **14 days**. Self-Assessment required. Must obtain LSPr-certified Tourism Business Standard. Health Feasibility Certificate. TKA documentation required if employing foreign workers. Authority: Gubernur.

**Tier 3 — Mikro/Kecil**: Medium-High risk (Menengah Tinggi). NIB + Standard Certificate within **14 days**. Same LSPr certification and Health Certificate requirements. Authority: Gubernur.

**Important:** Even Mikro-scale hotels carry Medium-High risk under Tier 3 — there is NO low-risk path for any hotel operation regardless of size.

**Post-issuance obligations across all tiers:**
- Obtain a Health Feasibility Certificate (Sertifikat Laik Sehat)
- Obtain an Alcohol Direct Sales Certificate (SKPL A, B, or C) if serving alcohol
- Submit Self-Assessment Document (Dokumen Penilaian Mandiri Kesiapan Penerapan Standar usaha Hotel Bintang)

**PMA Status:** Fully open (Terbuka) — 100% foreign ownership.

**Source Regulation:** PP 28/2025, Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, 14/2024.
55104.whatChanged: CODICE_RINUMERATO. This code has been renumbered and split from the older KBLI 2020 code 55110 (Hotel Bintang) to specifically isolate two-star hotel classifications.
55104.baliContext: Two-star hotels in Bali frequently take the shape of premium surf camps, digital nomad lodges, or boutique budget stays in hotspots like Batu Bolong, Padang Padang, and central Ubud. Setting up a formal hotel requires robust zoning compliance; your land must be located in a commercial or tourism zone (Kawasan Pariwisata). Unlike a simple villa, a two-star hotel involves 24/7 operational overheads, staff facilities, and heavy scrutiny over commercial building permits (PBG). Expect construction costs for a typical 20-room lodge in a secondary location to start around IDR 5-8 billion, plus a hefty land lease (Hak Sewa) running IDR 15-25 million per are per year. Navigating local banjar relations is essential if you plan to secure an alcohol permit (SKPL) for your pool bar.

**Post-issuance obligations:**

55105.baliContext: In the Bali ecosystem, a one-star hotel is often the legal classification used for high-end backpacker hostels, upscale guesthouses, or 'kos-kosan elit' (elite boarding houses) that transition into daily tourist rentals. It is a highly profitable, high-turnover model in dense areas like Legian, Tuban, and central Denpasar. While cheaper to build than a 2-star property, it still requires formal LSPr (Tourism Certification Body) audits. A common trap for foreign investors is treating this like a small homestay; the OSS system views it as a formal commercial hotel, meaning your environmental documents (SPPL/UKL-UPL) and wastewater management (IPAL) will be strictly monitored by the local environmental agency (DLHK).

55201.whatItMeans: Homestays — short-term accommodation in a residential building where the owner actually lives in the same house. You rent out rooms in your home to guests, giving them a chance to experience local life. The owner is present and the building is primarily a residence, not a purpose-built hotel.
55201.whatYouNeed:
**Micro + Small + Medium**: Medium-Low risk. NIB + Standard Certificate issued **automatically**. You need a Health Feasibility Certificate (Sertifikat Laik Sehat) and must submit periodic activity reports.

**PMA:** Fully open — 100% foreign ownership. Though in practice, homestays are overwhelmingly local businesses.

Note: PP28 data maps from old code 80100, which was a mapping artifact — the licensing requirements are specific to accommodation.
55201.whatChanged: The 2025 code 55201 was renumbered (CODICE_RINUMERATO). In the PP28 mapping, it connects to 80100 — but that's a data artifact from the transition. The concept of homestay accommodation existed in KBLI 2020 and carries forward. The key difference is the 2025 classification system now clearly separates homestays from villas, hotels, and other accommodation types.
55201.baliContext: Homestays are the heart of Balinese tourism hospitality. The banjar (village council) system means your neighbors know if you're hosting guests — and community approval matters as much as government licensing. Ubud pioneered the homestay movement. Munduk, Sidemen, Amed, and Pemuteran have growing homestay scenes catering to the 'authentic Bali' crowd. Keep in mind: Bali's awig-awig (customary village rules) can impose additional conditions — some banjars require a contribution or approval before you can host tourists. Also, your building must genuinely be a residence where the owner lives, not a converted villa pretending to be a homestay.

- 79110 — If you arrange tours or transport for guests

55203.whatItMeans: Villas — private houses exclusively rented out to tourists, with facilities, managed by the owner. Unlike a homestay (55201), the owner does not live on the same property. These are dedicated short-stay rental properties: the classic Bali villa experience with a private pool, tropical garden, and often resident staff. One villa or an entire compound — this is the code.
55203.whatYouNeed:
**Micro + Small + Medium**: Medium-Low risk (Menengah Rendah). NIB + Sertifikat Standar issued **automatically** via OSS (Otomatis).

**Scale note:** PP28/2025 lists no Skala Besar (Large-scale) entry for 55203. This does not restrict PMA — it simply means large-scale villa operations aren't separately categorised. A PT PMA with IDR 10B+ investment operates under the Medium scale licensing regime regardless of physical size. Perpres 10/2021 keeps the sector fully open to 100% foreign ownership at all operational sizes.

**Step-by-step to operate legally:**
1. **PT PMA incorporation** — notary deed, AHU registration, TDP (~2–4 weeks, IDR 8–15M notary fees)
2. **NIB via OSS** — register on oss.go.id, select 55203, auto-issued (1–3 days)
3. **Sertifikat Standar** — auto-issued with NIB for Menengah Rendah
4. **KKPR** (Kesesuaian Kegiatan Pemanfaatan Ruang) — spatial conformity, from ATR/BPN (2–6 weeks, if land zoning requires it)
5. **PBG** (Persetujuan Bangunan Gedung) — building permit, replaces IMB since 2022 (4–12 weeks)
6. **Sertifikat Laik Sehat** — health feasibility certificate from Dinas Kesehatan (2–4 weeks)
7. **Tanda Daftar Usaha Pariwisata (TDUP)** — tourism business registration from Dinas Pariwisata Kabupaten

**Typical total timeline:** 3–5 months from PT PMA to fully operational.
**Minimum PT PMA capital:** IDR 10 billion stated capital (Rp 2.5B paid-up).

**Authority:** Bupati/Walikota (district/city level).
**PMA:** Fully open — 100% foreign ownership. No local partner required.
55203.whatChanged: Renumbered from 55193 in KBLI 2020 to 55203 in 2025 (CODICE_RINUMERATO). PP28 licensing data maps from old code 55193 with a 100% match — same risk level, same permits, same obligations. No substantive change for operators: if you are running under 55193, the transition to 55203 is administrative only.
55203.baliContext:
**🏝 The Bali Villa Market (Reality Check)**
- Villas ARE Bali's tourism identity: Seminyak, Canggu, Ubud, Uluwatu, Sanur — every area has its scene
- Most popular accommodation KBLI for foreign investors by volume
- Typical structure: PT PMA leases land (Hak Sewa, 25–30 years), builds villa, rents on Airbnb/Booking.com
- **Oversupply warning:** Canggu and Seminyak have thousands of villas competing for the same guests; occupancy rates have dropped significantly since 2022
- **Better ROI areas (2025):** Tabanan, Sidemen (Karangasem), Amed, north coast — lower land prices, growing demand

---

**⚠ Common Mistakes That Kill the Business**
- **Operating without TDUP** — Dinas Pariwisata enforcement intensified in 2023–2024; fines and closure orders have been executed in Canggu, Pererenan, and Seminyak
- **Building before PBG** — IMB/PBG crackdowns since 2024 have resulted in actual demolition orders in Bali
- **Skipping Sertifikat Laik Sehat** — required for legal operation; without it your NIB is valid but your villa is not
- **Ignoring the banjar** — local village council approval is not a government permit but is socially and operationally essential; no banjar consent = neighbor problems, access issues, staff walkouts
- **Nominee land ownership** — still common, still illegal; BPN and PPATK have increased scrutiny on nominee arrangements since 2023
55203.youllAlsoNeed:
- **56101** — If you provide food service (in-villa chef, breakfast, restaurant)
- **68112** — For the property lease/rental structure (if your PT PMA also holds the lease)
- **96230** — If you offer spa or massage services at the villa
- **79110** — If you arrange tours, activities, or transfers for guests
- **77311** — If you rent out motorbikes, scooters, or vehicles to guests
- **41012** — If your PT PMA also builds/constructs the villa itself

55204.whatItMeans: Serviced apartments — apartments managed and operated as hotels for short-term stays, with payment calculated per-night or per-period. Think aparthotel (apartel) or condotel (kondotel). The unit is an apartment by design, but it functions as a hotel room: housekeeping, front desk, daily rates. This is *not* a long-term residential lease — it's hospitality accommodation in apartment form.

Post-issuance obligations:
- Obtain a Health Feasibility Certificate (Sertifikat Laik Sehat)
- Obtain a tourism business standard certificate from an accredited LSPr (Sertifikat Standar Usaha Pariwisata dari Lembaga Sertifikasi Profesi)

**Authority:** Governor (Gubernur) — provincial level, not Bupati/Walikota. This signals a higher regulatory bar than villas or homestays.

**PMA:** Fully open (Terbuka) — 100% foreign ownership.

The key difference from villas (55203): aparthotels carry **Medium-High** risk, require Governor-level approval, and need LSPr certification — villas are Medium-Low with automatic issuance.
55204.baliContext: Aparthotels are growing fast in Bali, especially in Seminyak, Kuta, and the Canggu-Berawa corridor. The model is popular with developers: build apartment units, sell them to individual investors, then manage the entire building as a hotel — the owner gets rental income, the operator runs it like a hotel. Condotels in Bali have been controversial (many buyers felt misled about returns), but the model persists because it works for both parties when managed well. Regulatory scrutiny is increasing — the Governor-level licensing reflects this. Occupancy can be excellent in prime locations (70-85% in peak season), but the per-night rate is typically lower than equivalent star-rated hotels. The sweet spot is lifestyle travelers who want a kitchen, washing machine, and living space but still want hotel services. Canggu and Uluwatu are seeing the newest developments in this category.

- 55101-55106 — If any units are classified as star-rated hotel rooms
- 68112 — For the underlying property lease/rental structure
- 96230 — If you offer spa or wellness services
- 93116 — If you include gym/fitness facilities
- 55400 — If you list on OTAs (accommodation intermediary activity)

55209.whatItMeans: Catch-all for short-stay accommodation NOT classified elsewhere. Explicitly includes: bungalows, cottages without daily cleaning, mountain lodges, hostels, capsule hotels, tree houses, cabins, glamping. Does NOT include daily/weekly hotel services.
55209.whatYouNeed:

55209.whatChanged: CODICE_RINUMERATO from 55199. IMPORTANT: this code now explicitly lists 'glamping' in its definition, partially overlapping with 55300 (Camping Grounds). The distinction: 55209 covers the accommodation STRUCTURE (the glamping unit itself), while 55300 covers the SITE (the camping ground as a managed area).
55209.baliContext: This is the 'innovation catch-all' for Bali's accommodation sector. Capsule hotels in Kuta, tree houses in Ubud, shipping container hotels in Canggu, eco-lodges in Sidemen — if it doesn't fit standard categories, it's 55209. The code's flexibility is its strength: new accommodation concepts don't need regulatory reclassification. HOWEVER, zoning still applies — tourism zoning required regardless of structure type. The Medium-Low risk makes this one of the easiest hospitality entry points. For PMA investors, the challenge is demonstrating IDR 10B investment value for what are often deliberately low-capex concepts.

55300.whatItMeans: Open-air accommodation using tents or caravans brought by travelers. Covers: recreational campgrounds, fishing/hunting camps, caravan parks, shelters, plain bivouac facilities. Does NOT cover accommodation booking intermediary services.
55300.whatYouNeed:

55300.whatChanged: CODICE_RINUMERATO from 55192. Functionally the same — campgrounds remain campgrounds.
55300.baliContext: GLAMPING BOOM AND BUST. This is the hottest — and most dangerous — investment category in 2025/2026 Bali. The appeal is obvious: lower capex than permanent structures, high Instagram appeal, nature-integrated tourism. THE CRITICAL ZONING MYTH: Many investors believe that because glamping structures are 'temporary' (no concrete foundation), they can build in Green Zones (LSD - Lahan Sawah Dilindungi / Protected Rice Fields). THIS IS FALSE. Commercial accommodation REQUIRES Tourism Zoning (Pink/Orange Zone) regardless of structure type. The OSS/GISTARU digital integration automatically rejects KBLI 55300 on agricultural land. ENFORCEMENT: Recent demolitions in Tabanan and East Bali targeted riverside/cliffside glamping sites violating sempadan (setback) rules. Unlike permanent buildings, glamping structures are legally easy to dismantle — making swift demolition orders common. UKL-UPL (Environmental Impact) compliance is mandatory, especially regarding waste management in ecologically sensitive areas.
55300.youllAlsoNeed:
- 55209 — Other Short-Stay (for the glamping units themselves)
- 93294 — Cave/Hot Spring/Nature Adventure (for adventure activities)
- 93296 — Agro Tourism (if on agricultural land — but SEE ZONING WARNINGS)
- 56101 — Restaurant (for on-site dining)
55300.zantaraOpener: Glamping is Bali's hottest accommodation trend — but 55300 carries severe zoning risks that have shut down dozens of sites.

55400.whatItMeans: Accommodation Intermediary Services — operating as the middleman between property owners and guests. This covers digital booking platforms (OTAs), villa management marketing agencies, and time-share exchanges that connect clients to accommodations for a fee or commission. It does not include companies that physically operate the properties or combine bookings with holiday tour packages.

This code exists in KBLI 2025 but has no PP28/2025 licensing data yet (BPS_ONLY). Requirements will be published when OSS integrates KBLI 2025.

55400.whatChanged: BPS_ONLY. This is a brand new code in the 2025 update, specifically created to capture the massive growth of digital accommodation booking platforms and property management intermediaries.
55400.baliContext: This is a massive regulatory win for Bali's booming "villa management" sector. Previously, digital booking agents and OTA startups in Canggu and Seminyak had to squeeze their business models into vague 'Web Portal' or heavy 'Travel Agency' codes. If your business model involves taking a 15-20% commission to market villas on Airbnb or Booking.com, handling guest communications, and facilitating payments—without actually owning the leaseholds—this is your dedicated code. Because it is a digital intermediary service, you will eventually be required to register as an Electronic System Provider (PSE) with Kominfo. It's a highly scalable, capital-light business model ideal for tech-savvy expats.

55901.baliContext: THIS IS THE 'MISSING LINK' CODE. 55901 legalizes the widespread but often unlicensed practice of villa management companies. Hundreds of Bali businesses manage villas on behalf of absent owners — handling check-ins, cleaning, maintenance, Airbnb listings, guest communication. Previously, this was done informally. Under KBLI 2025, any entity managing accommodation for others MUST hold this code. For PMA investors, this offers a SCALABLE business model: manage 50-100 villas without owning the underlying land or buildings. The management fee structure (typically 20-30% of rental income) creates recurring revenue without property risk. Compare with 68292 (Real Estate Management) which covers the property itself rather than the hospitality operation.

56101.whatItMeans: This is your classic restaurant code — any place that serves food in a permanent building. Sit-down restaurants, warungs with concrete walls, fast food joints, food courts inside malls, even hotel restaurants. If people walk in, sit down, and eat food you cooked in a fixed building, this is the code.
56101.whatYouNeed:
**Micro scale** (smallest operations): Medium-Low risk. You get your NIB + Standard Certificate automatically — no waiting. You'll need a Hygiene Sanitation Label (HSP) and must submit periodic activity reports.

**Small / Medium / Large scale**: Medium-High risk. NIB + Standard Certificate issued within **14 working days**. You'll need a Self-Assessment of Standard Readiness, a certified standard from an LSPr (certification body), and a Hygiene Sanitation Feasibility Certificate (SLHS).

**PMA (foreign investment):** Fully open — 100% foreign ownership allowed.
56101.whatChanged: Big change in 2025. The old 56101 (restaurants) got merged with three other codes: 56103 (food stalls/tents), 56104 (self-service restaurants), and 56109 (other fixed-building food). So if you had a cafeteria-style or self-service setup under a separate code before, it's all 56101 now. One code to rule them all for fixed-building food service.
56101.baliContext: This is the single most common business code for foreigners in Bali. Seminyak, Canggu, and Ubud are saturated — the competition is fierce and landlords know it. Sanur and Uluwatu still have room. Keep in mind: Bali's health department (Dinas Kesehatan) does actual inspections for your SLHS, and they check kitchen hygiene, water quality, and food storage. Budget 2-4 weeks for the inspection alone. Also, most Bali restaurants need a separate liquor license if they serve alcohol — 56101 alone doesn't cover that.
56101.youllAlsoNeed:
- 56301 — If you serve alcohol (bar license, required for cocktails and spirits)
- 56303 — If you also operate as a café/coffee shop
- 47221 — If you sell retail beverages (bottled drinks to go)
- 68112 — If you're leasing the building yourself

56102.whatItMeans: Food service from non-permanent structures — food trucks, mobile warung, market stalls, pop-up food stands, and street food carts operating as a formal business entity. The defining legal characteristic is **bangunan tidak tetap** (non-permanent structure): the food preparation and serving facility is not a fixed building. If your kitchen is on wheels, in a tent, at a market kiosk, or at a temporary stall, this is your code. This is categorically different from 56101 (restaurant in a permanent building). A PT PMA running an artisan food truck concept — specialty coffee, gourmet burgers, craft ice cream, fusion street food — operates under this code.
56102.whatYouNeed:
**All scales (Mikro/Kecil/Menengah/Besar): Low Risk (Rendah)**
NIB + Sertifikat Standar issued **automatically** (Otomatis) via OSS. Authority: **Bupati/Walikota** (district/city level).

**Post-issuance obligations:**
- **Label Higiene Sanitasi Pangan (HSP)** — mandatory. This is a **label** (simpler declaration), NOT the full Sertifikat SLHS (Sertifikat Laik Higiene Sanitasi) required for permanent restaurants. Issued by Dinas Kesehatan after basic inspection; faster and lower cost than the SLHS.
- **Laporan berkala** — periodic activity reports to Bupati/Walikota
- No alcohol sales without **SKPL** (Surat Keterangan Penjualan Langsung) — food trucks are typically non-alcoholic; if you want to serve beer or wine at a pop-up, this requires a separate permit

**Note on Label HSP vs Sertifikat SLHS:**
- Label HSP = simpler food hygiene declaration for mobile/non-permanent operations; issued after a basic hygiene inspection
- Sertifikat SLHS = full health feasibility certification for permanent restaurant (56101); more complex and takes longer
- Using 56102 with Label HSP is the fast, correct path for food trucks; do not apply for SLHS if your structure is non-permanent

**Step-by-step for PT PMA food truck:**
1. **PT PMA incorporation** — notary deed, AHU registration; IDR 10B stated capital (~3–5 weeks)
2. **NIB via OSS** — select 56102; auto-issued 1–3 days
3. **Label HSP** — apply to Dinas Kesehatan kabupaten/kota; basic hygiene inspection of your mobile unit (~2–4 weeks)
4. **Operational permits for location** — depending on where you operate:
   - Public market/bazaar: letter from market management
   - Road-side: Izin Gangguan (if required by local regulation) from Satpol PP
   - Beach area: Izin from Dinas Pariwisata or Dinas Kelautan for beach/coastal zones
   - Private venue (beach club, event): venue's own permit covers you as tenant
5. **PIRT** (Produksi Industri Rumah Tangga) — if producing packaged food items (bottled sauces, packaged products) for sale alongside your truck; issued by Dinas Kesehatan separately

**Typical total timeline:** 4–8 weeks from PT PMA to operational.
**Minimum PT PMA capital:** IDR 10 billion stated capital (Rp 2.5B paid-up).

**PMA:** Fully open (Terbuka) — 100% foreign ownership.
56102.whatChanged: Direct match from KBLI 2020 (MATCH_LANGSUNG). Code and scope unchanged — 56102 has always covered non-permanent food structures. The distinction between Label HSP (56102) and Sertifikat SLHS (56101) was clarified in PP28/2025's updated obligation framework. The food truck and pop-up culture has grown dramatically since 2020 but the legal framework is the same code.
56102.baliContext:
**🚚 The Bali Food Truck & Market Stall Scene (2025)**

**What's working:**
- **Canggu food truck culture:** The Berawa/Batu Bolong corridor has 3–5 active food truck parks; specialty coffee trucks, Japanese-inspired street food, and gourmet burgers are common formats
- **Seminyak night markets and pop-ups:** Weekend bazaars and rooftop pop-up events rotate vendors; 56102 is the legal structure for all of them
- **Beach club vendor slots:** Finns, Tropicola, and similar venues rent stall/vendor spots to external F&B operators; you need 56102 + Label HSP to legally operate in these spaces
- **Festival and event catering:** BIAF (Bali International Art Festival), Ubud Writers Festival, local festivals — the event catering market requires 56210 for contracted catering but 56102 for a stall/stand format

**PMA food truck concept — what actually works:**
- Specialty single-product concept: matcha soft serve, authentic NY-style pizza, Korean fried chicken — works when there's genuine product differentiation from local warung
- Mobile specialty coffee with roaster story: Bali's coffee culture supports premium positioning; mobile format lowers barrier vs permanent café
- Artisan ice cream with local ingredients: Kintamani coffee, Bali vanilla, salak — tourist segment pays premium for 'local + premium' positioning

**Revenue reality:**
- A well-positioned food truck/stall in Canggu or Seminyak: IDR 5–25M/day in sales (high season)
- Beach club vendor slot rent: IDR 2–5M/day site fee + % of revenue to venue
- Weekend market stall: IDR 500K–2M/day site fee; IDR 3–10M sales on strong market days

---

**⚠ Key Issues**
- **Location permit is location-specific** — Label HSP covers your unit; where you park/operate requires separate location authorization; beach/coastal sites are strictly controlled by Dinas Pariwisata and sometimes require KKPR clearance
- **Fire safety for mobile kitchens** — gas cylinder storage and ventilation in food trucks requires compliance with DAMKAR (Dinas Pemadam Kebakaran) standards; annual inspection recommended
- **No alcohol without SKPL** — even if the beach club next to you serves drinks, your truck cannot; get SKPL if your concept includes alcohol service
56102.youllAlsoNeed:
- **56101** — Restaurant in permanent building (if you later open a fixed location alongside the truck)
- **56210** — Event Catering (if you also provide contracted catering for events — different code from stall/truck)
- **47211** — Retail Food (if selling packaged food products alongside the food service)
- **77319** — Vehicle/Equipment Rental (if renting out the food truck itself to others)

The key distinction from a restaurant (56101): Label HSP instead of full SLHS certification, and your location permit is separate from your operating permit. 56210.whatItMeans: Event catering — preparing and delivering food for specific occasions at a location chosen by the client. Weddings, corporate events, private parties, conference lunches, villa catering for guests. You cook it in your kitchen, transport it to the event location, serve it there. This is contract-based food service, NOT a walk-in restaurant. The critical distinction from 56101 (restaurant): no permanent dining room for walk-in customers.
56210.whatYouNeed:
**Mikro + Kecil scale**: Medium-Low risk (Menengah Rendah). NIB + Sertifikat Standar issued **automatically** (Otomatis). Authority: **Bupati/Walikota** (district level).

**Menengah + Besar scale**: Medium-High risk (Menengah Tinggi). NIB + Sertifikat Standar issued within **14 working days**. Authority: **Gubernur** (provincial level).

**Step-by-step for a PT PMA event catering business:**
1. **PT PMA incorporation** — notary deed, AHU registration (~2–4 weeks)
2. **Commercial kitchen facility** — lease or build a licensed kitchen (does NOT need to be a restaurant; can be production kitchen only) (~4–12 weeks)
3. **PBG (building permit)** — if constructing or renovating kitchen facility (~8–16 weeks)
4. **Kitchen build-out** — commercial-grade equipment, health standards compliance (~2–4 months)
5. **NIB via OSS** — register on oss.go.id, select 56210; Mikro/Kecil = auto-issued; Menengah/Besar = 14 days
6. **Dokumen Penilaian Mandiri** — self-assessment of readiness to implement food safety standards (Menengah/Besar scale)
7. **Sertifikat Standar Usaha Pariwisata** — tourism business standard certificate from LSPr (Menengah/Besar scale only) (~4–8 weeks)
8. **Label Higiene Sanitasi Pangan (HSP)** — food hygiene label from Dinas Kesehatan; kitchen inspection (Mikro/Kecil scale) (~2–4 weeks)
9. **Sertifikat Laik Higiene Sanitasi (SLHS)** — full health feasibility certificate (Menengah/Besar scale) (~2–4 weeks)
10. **Marketing and partnerships** — build relationships with wedding planners, villa management companies, corporate event organizers

**Typical total timeline:** 4–8 months from PT PMA to first event.

**Post-issuance obligations:**
- Maintain kitchen hygiene standards (HSP or SLHS depending on scale)
- Submit periodic reports to Bupati/Walikota or Gubernur
- Renew health certificates annually

**Authority:** Bupati/Walikota (Mikro/Kecil) or Gubernur (Menengah/Besar).
**PMA:** Fully open — 100% foreign ownership. No restrictions.

**Source Regulation:** PP 28/2025, Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, 14/2024.
56210.whatChanged: Direct match from KBLI 2020 (MATCH_LANGSUNG). Event catering code unchanged. The distinction from 56101 (restaurant) is clearer in 2025: 56210 = no permanent dining room; 56101 = permanent dining room for walk-in customers. If you have both (restaurant + catering), you need both codes.
56210.baliContext:
**💒 The Bali Wedding Catering Market (Reality Check)**
- Destination wedding capital of Southeast Asia: 3,000–5,000 international weddings/year in Bali
- Top venues: Uluwatu cliff-top (Tirtha Uluwatu, Alila Villas), Ubud rice terraces (Kamandalu, Viceroy), beachfront Nusa Dua (Mulia, St. Regis)
- Average wedding catering contract: IDR 150–500M (50–200 guests; USD 300–800/pax all-in)
- Peak season: April–October (dry season); booking 12–18 months in advance

---

**⚠ CRITICAL: Distinction from 56101 (Restaurant)**
- **56210 (Event Catering)** = production kitchen + mobile service; NO permanent dining room for walk-in customers
- **56101 (Restaurant)** = permanent dining room where customers walk in and order
- If you have BOTH (restaurant that also does catering), you need BOTH codes on your NIB
- Many operators start with 56210 only (lower overhead; no dining room rent/staff)

**⚠ Wedding Market Entry Strategies**
- **Venue partnerships** — most high-end venues have exclusive or preferred caterer lists; breaking in requires relationship-building + trial events
- **Villa catering niche** — 1,000+ private villas in Bali; many offer in-villa chef/catering services to guests; this is a B2B2C model (you contract with villa management, they sell to guests)
- **Specialty positioning** — authentic Italian (wood-fired pizza, fresh pasta), Japanese (sushi/sashimi quality), plant-based luxury (vegan fine dining) — works if genuinely differentiated
- **Corporate events** — MICE market (conferences, retreats, team-building); lower per-pax spend (IDR 150–300K) but higher volume and repeat business

**⚠ Revenue Model Reality**
- Wedding catering: high margin (40–50% gross) but seasonal and unpredictable
- Villa catering: lower margin (25–35%) but steadier volume; villa management takes 20–30% commission
- Corporate events: lowest margin (20–30%) but most predictable; annual contracts possible
- Successful caterers in Bali run mixed model: weddings for margin, corporate for cash flow, villa partnerships for base volume

**⚠ Operational Requirements**
- **Commercial kitchen** — can be standalone production facility (not a restaurant); many caterers operate from industrial zones (Kerobokan, Denpasar outskirts) where rent is lower
- **Transport and logistics** — refrigerated van essential for food safety; Bali's traffic means 2–3 hour buffer for Ubud/Uluwatu deliveries from Seminyak kitchen
- **Event staffing** — waiters, bartenders, kitchen support hired per-event; labor cost = 15–25% of contract value
- **Equipment rental** — tables, chairs, glassware, linens usually rented per-event unless you're doing 50+ events/year

**⚠ Competition and Market Saturation**
- 50+ established catering companies in Bali (2025)
- Top-tier operators: Bali Catering Company, Kudus Catering, Tugu Catering — these dominate luxury wedding market
- Mid-tier: 20–30 companies competing on price and specialty cuisine
- Entry barrier: reputation and portfolio; first 10 events are critical for building credibility
56210.youllAlsoNeed:
- **56101** — Restaurant (if you also have a permanent dining room open to walk-in customers)
- **56301** — Bar (if your catering includes dedicated bar service with alcohol)
- **82300** — Event organizing (if you package catering as part of full event planning services)
- **77319** — Equipment rental (if you also rent out tables, chairs, tents for events)
- **68112** — Property rental (if your PT PMA holds the kitchen facility lease)

56290.baliContext: B2B catering is a stable, unglamorous business in Bali. Hotels outsource banquet catering, tech coworking spaces need daily lunch programs, international schools contract meal providers. Cloud kitchen operations for food delivery apps also fall here. Less location-sensitive than consumer venues — can operate from industrial/mixed zones. Lower community friction (no noise, no tourist crowds). For PMA investors, the IDR 10B minimum makes this viable only at scale — think corporate catering serving 5+ clients, not a single kitchen.

56301.whatItMeans: Bars — places where the main business is serving drinks, both alcoholic (spirits, beer, wine, whisky) and non-alcoholic. This includes beach clubs where drinks are the primary offering, bars on trains or boats, and any establishment where beverages are the star and food is secondary.
56301.whatYouNeed:
**Medium + Large scale only** (no Micro/Small entries): Medium-High risk. NIB + Standard Certificate within **14 working days**. You need a Self-Assessment of Standard Readiness document, LSPr-certified standard, and a Health Feasibility Certificate (Sertifikat Laik Sehat).

**PMA:** Fully open — 100% foreign ownership.

Note: There's no Micro/Small scale licensing path in the data. Bars are regulated at Medium scale and above.
56301.whatChanged: Unchanged from KBLI 2020 — direct match (MATCH_LANGSUNG). Bar is still bar.
56301.baliContext: Bali's bar and beach club scene is legendary — Seminyak's Jl. Petitenget, Canggu's Batu Bolong, Uluwatu's cliff-top venues. The key wrinkle: you need a separate alcohol distribution license (SIUP-MB) on top of this KBLI code. The alcohol license comes from the provincial trade office and can take 2-6 months. Beach clubs like Potato Head, Finns, and La Brisa all operate under this code. Important: Bali has periodic alcohol restriction discussions around Nyepi and religious holidays — stay informed about local regulations. Also, noise complaints from banjar (village councils) can shut you down faster than any government agency.

56302.whatItMeans: Night clubs — establishments primarily serving beverages alongside dance facilities, live music, and light shows. Includes hostesses/attendants for VIP service and entertainment acts. This is NOT just a bar with music — it's a specifically defined nightlife category with spettacoli (shows) and operational reality checks.
56302.whatYouNeed:
**Medium/Large scale ONLY** (no Micro/Small). Medium-High risk. NIB + Standard Certificate verified within **14 days**. Must obtain LSPr certification and Sertifikat Laik Sehat.

**CRITICAL:** Requires SKPL-A (or B and C) alcohol license — subject to strict regional quotas. Authority: Governor (not local Bupati).

**PMA:** Fully open — 100% foreign ownership allowed.
56302.whatChanged: MATCH_LANGSUNG — code unchanged, but enforcement has dramatically intensified since 2024.
56302.baliContext: THIS IS THE MOST DANGEROUS CODE IN BALI. Satpol PP (Public Order Enforcement) now classifies venues by operational reality, not license text. If you have a DJ booth, dance floor, and ticketed entry, you ARE 56302 regardless of what your NIB says. CRITICAL ZONING: 56302 is PROHIBITED in Yellow (Residential) and Green (Agricultural) zones. Requires specific Tourism/Entertainment Zoning. Many Canggu venues operated as 'restaurants' (56101) or 'bars' while functioning as nightclubs — these face immediate closure when audited. The SKPL alcohol license is a scarce, quota-controlled asset in saturated areas like Seminyak. Noise regulations (decibel limits) are now actively enforced with professional measurement equipment.
56302.youllAlsoNeed:
- 56301 — Bar (safer alternative if no dance floor)
- 56101 — Restaurant (if also serving food)
- 93291 — Dance Venue (for dedicated dance events)
- 56305 — Herbal/Jamu Shop (NOT a bar — see note)

56303.whatItMeans: Discotheques — pure dance music venues focused on DJ performances, electronic music, and clubbing experiences. Unlike night clubs (56302) which feature live shows and spettacoli, discotheques focus on recorded music, DJ sets, and dance floor atmosphere without structured entertainment acts.
56303.whatYouNeed:
**All scales (Micro through Large)**: Medium-Low risk. NIB + Standard Certificate issued **automatically** — no waiting period for any scale. PMA businesses need an LSPr-certified standard. You'll need a Self-Assessment document covering facilities, organization, and HR.

**PMA:** Fully open — 100% foreign ownership.

56303.baliContext: Bali's discotheque scene centers on DJ culture and electronic music venues. Unlike night clubs with live shows, discotheques focus on pure dance floor experiences with professional sound systems and lighting. The good news: 56303 is one of the easier F&B codes to get — Medium-Low risk at ALL scales, automatic issuance. The bad news: exactly because it's easy, competition is brutal. Ubud's Jl. Goutama, Canggu's Pantai Berawa, and Seminyak's backstreets are all oversaturated. Consider emerging areas like Amed, Sidemen, or Tabanan if you want breathing room. Technical infrastructure (DJ booths, sound systems, lighting) is critical — budget accordingly for your Technical Manager.

Audio equipment quality is critical — guests expect professional sound systems and extensive song libraries. The barrier to entry is relatively low for small venues, but larger karaoke establishments require significant audio/video infrastructure investment. Securing the Food Hygiene and Sanitation Label (HSP) from the local health department is essential. Ensure proper soundproofing to avoid noise complaints from neighboring properties.

**Large scale**: Medium-High risk. NIB + Standard Certificate within **14 working days**. Full compliance documentation, including TDUP, Self-Assessment of Standard Readiness, and LSPr-certified standard.

**PMA:** Fully open — 100% foreign ownership allowed.

59112.baliContext: Bali is a magnet for international productions — the landscapes, the light, the relatively low crew costs compared to Australia or Europe. Foreign productions shooting in Bali need a separate Shooting Permit (Izin Pengambilan Gambar) from the regional film board on top of this KBLI code. Ubud, Uluwatu cliffs, and rice terrace locations in Tegallalang are perennial favorites. Local crew talent is strong for camera and grip departments but thin for specialized VFX work. Budget 2-4 weeks for permit processing if you're planning a commercial shoot.
59112.youllAlsoNeed:

- 59201 — Sound Recording (if you also run a recording studio)
- 59140 — Cinema Operation (if you screen your own films)

- 74100 — Specialized Design (for production design services)
59112.zantaraOpener: Producing film or video content in Bali? 59112 is your production code — but you'll also need a separate Shooting Permit for location work.

59140.whatItMeans: Cinema operation — running movie theaters, screening rooms, and film exhibition venues. This covers traditional cinemas, boutique screening rooms, open-air movie nights, and drive-in theaters. The business is showing films to a paying audience, not making them. If you project it on a screen and sell tickets, this is the code.
59140.whatYouNeed:
**All scales (Micro / Small / Medium / Large)**: Low risk (Rendah). NIB only — no Standard Certificate required at any scale. This is unusually permissive for a public-facing entertainment venue. Bali's banjar system means noise and crowd management matter: get your neighbors on board before hosting outdoor screenings. The SLF (building certificate) process for public entertainment venues in Bali typically takes 1-3 months through the local DPMPTSP office.

59201.whatItMeans: Sound recording and music publishing — running a recording studio, producing music, publishing songs, and distributing sound recordings. This also covers the 'aggregator' model: companies that act as intermediaries between independent artists and streaming platforms like Spotify or Apple Music. If you record it, publish it, or distribute it, this is the code.
59201.whatYouNeed:
**All scales (Micro / Small / Medium / Large)**: Low risk (Rendah). NIB only — no Standard Certificate required at any scale. This makes sound recording one of the most frictionless creative industry codes to set up. No TDUP needed (that's specific to film), no LSPr certification, no waiting periods.

Studios in Canggu and Ubud cater to international artists recording in a tropical setting, and several music aggregator businesses operate from Bali serving Southeast Asian indie artists. The low-risk classification at all scales makes this an attractive entry point for creative entrepreneurs. Soundproofing is your main practical challenge — Bali's building standards don't account for studio acoustics, so budget for a proper build-out. The electronic music scene around Canggu creates natural demand for production and mastering services.

60103.whatItMeans: On-demand audio distribution and streaming services — music streaming, audio podcasts, audiobooks. Covers subscription-based and ad-supported models. 60103.whatYouNeed:
**ALL scales: High Risk (Tinggi).** NIB + full License (Izin). Processing takes up to **29 working days** (7 admin + 15 technical inspection + 7 fee verification).

Requires: broadcasting plan (background, revenue projections, shareholding structure, coverage map, facilities), board members not blacklisted, multiple sworn statements (compliance, frequency licensing, content regulation), operational feasibility test, broadcasting license fee payment within 15 days.

**Authority:** Minister / Agency Head.

**PMA:** Fully open — 100% foreign ownership allowed.
60103.whatChanged: CODICE_RINUMERATO from KBLI 2020 code 60102 (Private Radio Broadcasting). The name change is significant — KBLI 2025 explicitly separates on-demand streaming from traditional broadcasting, recognizing the digital shift. However, the licensing requirements inherited from broadcasting are arguably over-regulated for pure streaming services.
60103.baliContext: The High Risk classification and broadcasting-era licensing requirements make this one of the most heavily regulated digital media codes. For a Bali-based podcast network or music streaming startup, the 29-day approval process and broadcasting infrastructure requirements (coverage maps, frequency licensing) are significant barriers. Most Bali-based audio content creators operate under general IT or content codes to avoid the broadcasting regulatory framework. The Kominfo PSE (Private Electronic System Provider) registration is also required.

60203.whatItMeans: On-demand video distribution and streaming — VOD platforms, subscription/ad-based video streaming, digital video downloads, game streaming (view-only, not playable). Does NOT include traditional TV broadcasting.
60203.whatYouNeed:
**ALL scales: High Risk (Tinggi).** NIB + full License (Izin). Processing takes up to **29 working days** (7 admin + 15 technical inspection + 7 fee verification).

Same structure as 60103 — broadcasting plan, technical inspection, license fee. Additionally may require Satellite Mooring Rights (Hak Labuh Satelit) if using foreign satellites.

**Authority:** Minister / Agency Head.

**PMA:** Fully open — 100% foreign ownership allowed.
60203.whatChanged: CODICE_RINUMERATO from KBLI 2020 code 60202 (TV Programming & Broadcasting). Separates on-demand video from linear TV, but inherits the broadcasting regulatory burden.
60203.baliContext: Same regulatory challenges as 60103. For Bali-based video content creators, the High Risk classification is a major obstacle. The game streaming provision (view-only) is notable — it potentially covers Twitch-like platforms under this code rather than gaming codes. Most Bali-based content creators distribute via YouTube/Instagram (platform operators bear the regulatory burden) rather than building their own streaming platforms.

60390.whatItMeans: Social networking sites and content distribution/sharing platforms. Includes blogs, wikis, online gaming video sites, e-book distribution (non-publishing), and digital game intermediary services (vouchers, in-game items, premium access via marketplaces). A catch-all for social/sharing platforms.
60390.whatYouNeed:
**BPS_ONLY** — no PP28 risk assignment yet. Currently pending formal licensing framework. In practice, operators must register as PSE (Private Electronic System Provider) with Kominfo.

Likely will be classified as High Risk when PP28 integration occurs, given content moderation obligations.

**PMA:** Fully open — 100% foreign ownership allowed.
60390.whatChanged: BPS_ONLY — ENTIRELY NEW code in KBLI 2025. No direct predecessor. Previously social media platforms fell under web portal codes (63122) or were unclassified. The explicit inclusion of game item marketplaces and digital voucher sales is notable — Indonesia is acknowledging the digital goods economy.
60390.baliContext: The BPS_ONLY status makes this a 'watch and wait' code. Few Bali-based companies would build their own social media platforms, but the digital game marketplace provision is relevant for the gaming community. Content creators on existing platforms (YouTube, TikTok) do NOT need this code — it's for platform OPERATORS. The Kominfo PSE registration requirement applies regardless of PP28 status.
60390.youllAlsoNeed:
- 63101 — Data Processing (for platform infrastructure)
- 62199 — Software Development (for platform development)
- 73100 — Advertising (for ad revenue model)
- 62191 — E-Commerce App Development (if selling digital goods)
60390.zantaraOpener: Building a social platform or game marketplace? 60390 is Indonesia's new code for content distribution — still pending formal licensing requirements.

63101.whatYouNeed:
Three distinct licensing tiers from aggregated PP28 sources (63121, 63111):

**Tier 1 — Kecil/Menengah**: Low risk (Rendah). NIB only, issued **automatically**. Validated Industrial Data reports every 6 months. Data security SOPs. HR competency training certificates. Authority: Bupati/Walikota.

**Tier 2 — Kecil/Menengah**: Medium-Low risk (Menengah Rendah). NIB + Standard Certificate, issued **automatically**. Same data reporting obligations plus: equipment calibration certificates, organizational structure documentation showing qualified technical staff, and safety/security guarantees for tools and processes. Authority: Bupati/Walikota.

**Tier 3 — Besar**: Medium-High risk (Menengah Tinggi). NIB + Standard Certificate within **7 days**. Requires: organizational chart with qualified staff, employment contracts for at least 2 managers + 2 supervisors + 4 technical staff (permanent or minimum 1-year contract), business process flow documentation, equipment list with photos. Authority: Gubernur.

**Post-issuance obligations (all tiers):**
- Submit validated Industrial Data every 6 months (Data Industri tervalidasi)
- Maintain SOPs for data and electronic system security (SOP keamanan data dan sistem elektronik)
- Obtain HR competency training certificates (sertifikat pelatihan kompetensi SDM)

**PMA Status:** Fully open (Terbuka) — 100% foreign ownership.

**Source Regulation:** PP 28/2025 (aggregated from 63121, 63111).

64194.whatItMeans: Bank Perkreditan Rakyat (BPR) — Indonesia's rural/community bank providing basic banking services (savings, deposits, and credit) to local communities, SMEs, and individuals in their licensed geographic area. BPR cannot offer giro (checking accounts), cannot participate in national clearing, and cannot conduct international/foreign currency transactions — these are reserved for Umum banks. This is microfinance banking, not commercial banking. **TERBATAS (limited) foreign ownership: maximum 40% foreign shareholding.** Indonesian investors must hold at least 60%. OJK issues the BPR license — this is a full bank license process, not a standard OSS procedure.
64194.whatYouNeed:
**Risk: Tinggi.** The OSS process (NIB) is the administrative layer; the **OJK bank license is the operative requirement and takes 12–24 months.**

**Foreign ownership limit: maximum 40%.** This is a TERBATAS code — not fully open to PMA. Your Indonesian partner(s) must hold at least 60% of shares and be individuals or entities with proven financial capacity (fit & proper).

**Modal minimum by geographic category (per OJK POJK 5/2015 and updates):**
- **Wilayah Jabodetabek** (Jakarta Greater Area): IDR 16 miliar
- **Ibukota Provinsi** (Provincial capital, e.g., Denpasar): IDR 8 miliar
- **Kabupaten/Kota lain** (Other cities/regencies — most of Bali): IDR 6 miliar
- The entire capital must be paid up in full at time of OJK application

**TWO-PHASE process:**

**PHASE 1 — OSS / NIB:**
- Register PT (domestic structure required, since 60% must be Indonesian) on OSS
- Select 64194, Tinggi
- NIB issued; this does NOT authorize banking operations

**PHASE 2 — OJK BPR License (12–24 months):**
1. **Principle Approval (Izin Prinsip)** — initial OJK application showing founding shareholders, business plan, location; OJK evaluates feasibility (~3–6 months)
2. **Establishment (Pendirian)** — incorporate PT after Izin Prinsip; all shareholders must pass OJK fit & proper test
3. **Capital injection** — fully paid up in escrow; evidence submitted to OJK
4. **Physical premises** — OJK inspects the proposed office location; BPR cannot operate from virtual office
5. **Core Banking System** — OJK evaluates IT infrastructure; CBS must meet OJK POJK 75/2016 standards
6. **Director/Commissioner Fit & Proper** — OJK personally vets each director and commissioner
7. **Izin Usaha OJK** — issued after all stages clear; only then can BPR open to the public
8. **OJK ongoing supervision** — monthly financial reporting; annual audit by OJK-accredited auditor; Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) minimum 12%; NPL must not exceed 5%

**Geographic operational limit:** BPR may only operate within its licensed province. A Bali BPR cannot open branches in Java or Lombok without separate OJK approval.

**BPRS (Syariah) variant:** BPR Syariah follows sharia finance principles; governed by OJK and DSN-MUI; same capital requirements and foreign ownership limit of 40%.

**Typical full timeline:** 18–30 months from concept to first customer.
64194.whatChanged: Direct match from KBLI 2020 (MATCH_LANGSUNG). BPR was significantly restructured by **UU 4/2023 (P2SK Law)** which renamed BPR to 'Bank Perekonomian Rakyat' (keeping the same BPR acronym) and expanded the BPR product scope slightly. Key change: BPRs may now offer additional savings products and certain remittance services. The 40% foreign ownership cap is unchanged. OJK transferred BPR supervision fully from BI to OJK, which was completed in 2023.
64194.baliContext:
**🏦 BPR in Bali — The Microfinance Banking Layer**

**What BPR does that banks won't:**
- Provides loans of IDR 2–500 juta to UMKM operators, farmers, fishermen, village traders, and craftsmen who lack the collateral or documentation for commercial bank credit
- Accepts savings deposits from local community members (typically higher interest rate than bank savings, attracting local depositors)
- Processes faster than commercial banks — credit approval in 1–5 days vs 2–4 weeks for commercial bank SME loans

**Bali BPR landscape:**
- Bali has 130+ active BPRs (as of 2024) concentrated in Denpasar, Gianyar, Badung, and Tabanan
- Notable Bali BPRs: BPR Tish, BPR Dinar, BPR Sukawati Pancakanti (Gianyar focus), BPR Artha Hapat
- Competition is intense in south Bali; underpenetrated areas: Bangli, Karangasem (east Bali), Buleleng (north Bali)

**The 40% foreign + 60% Indonesian structure in practice:**
- Foreign investor contributes 40% equity (e.g., IDR 2.4 miliar of IDR 6 miliar minimum)
- Indonesian co-founder holds 60% (IDR 3.6 miliar) — must be a qualified individual or entity, not a nominee
- The Indonesian partner(s) must pass OJK fit & proper — no criminal record, no previous banking violations
- Common structure: experienced local Balinese banker (ex-BRI, ex-BNI) as 60% partner + foreign capital as 40% minority investor

**BPRS niche — halal microfinance for Middle Eastern tourism segment:**
- Bali receives increasing Middle Eastern and South Asian Muslim tourists
- A BPRS (Syariah) specifically serving halal-economy businesses (halal restaurants, Muslim-friendly homestays, abaya/modest fashion boutiques) = underexplored niche
- DSN-MUI sharia certification for products adds credibility

**⚠ Critical Issues**
- **40% cap is absolute** — OJK has rejected BPR applications where the foreign investor tried to exceed 40% through nominee structures; this is treated as fraud
- **Geographic restriction is real** — a Badung BPR cannot serve Ubud clients without opening a Gianyar branch (separate OJK approval); plan geographic scope from day one
- **NPL management is existential** — OJK places BPRs with NPL > 5% under enhanced supervision; NPL > 8% triggers OJK intervention; the BPR sector had 10+ forced mergers 2022–2024 due to NPL crises
64194.youllAlsoNeed:
- **64992** — Multifinance (if you want to add vehicle leasing or consumer goods financing to complement BPR micro-lending)
- **66191** — Fintech P2P Lending (for digital-first UMKM financing alongside the BPR physical branch model)
- **OJK legal counsel** — WAJIB — BPR license process requires specialized banking regulatory lawyer from Izin Prinsip through Izin Usaha; do not attempt without specialist legal support

64921.whatItMeans: Savings and loan cooperative (Koperasi Simpan Pinjam / KSP) — a member-owned financial cooperative that provides savings deposit facilities and credit/loans exclusively to its registered members. Only members can deposit; only members can borrow. This is structurally distinct from a bank (which serves the public) and from a multifinance company (which funds from capital markets). **CRITICAL: This code is TERTUTUP (closed) to foreign investment.** Only Indonesian legal entities and citizens (PMDN/WNI) may establish, own, or invest in a koperasi under Indonesian cooperative law. There is no PMA path into this structure. If your goal as a foreign investor is to serve the same underbanked UMKM market, your alternatives are: **66191** (fintech P2P lending, up to 85% foreign), **64992** (multifinance company, up to 85% foreign), or **64194** (BPR rural bank, up to 40% foreign).
64921.whatYouNeed:
**TERTUTUP — Foreign investment is not permitted under this code.**

This code is exclusively for Indonesian domestic entities (PMDN, WNI). The cooperative structure (badan hukum koperasi) is governed by UU 25/1992 (Perkoperasian) and cannot have foreign shareholders.

**For Indonesian founders (PMDN/WNI) establishing a KSP:**

Risk: Menengah Tinggi. Authority varies by geographic scope:
- **Bupati/Walikota** — for KSP operating within a single kabupaten/kota
- **Gubernur** — for KSP operating across multiple kabupaten within one province
- **Menteri** — for KSP operating across multiple provinces

Timeline: 7 working days for Sertifikat Standar (post-NIB).

**Steps for founding a KSP:**
1. **Founding meeting** — minimum 20 founding members required; draft AD/ART (anggaran dasar/rumah tangga)
2. **Notarial deed** — cooperative deed must be executed by a notaris
3. **Pengesahan Badan Hukum** — submission to Kemenkop UKM for legal entity approval (~30 days)
4. **NIB via OSS** — select 64921; risk Menengah Tinggi
5. **Sertifikat Standar** — submitted to Bupati/Walikota/Gubernur/Menteri depending on scope; 7 working day issuance
6. **OJK registration** — KSP that accept deposits above a threshold must register with OJK as LKNB (Lembaga Keuangan Non-Bank) under POJK 10/2016
7. **Operasional** — commence member recruitment, savings collection, and lending only after all permits are complete

**PMA alternatives (since 64921 is TERTUTUP):**
- **66191** — Fintech P2P lending (up to 85% foreign): technology-based lending platform connecting borrowers and lenders online; same UMKM financing gap, modern model
- **64992** — Multifinance (up to 85% foreign): vehicle leasing, UMKM working capital, property financing; IDR 100B minimum capital
- **64194** — BPR Rural Bank (maximum 40% foreign): traditional microbanking for local communities; OJK-licensed; IDR 6–16B minimum capital depending on location

The significant post-2020 development is OJK's expanded supervisory role over KSP following high-profile KSP collapses (KSP Indosurya 2020, KSP Sejahtera Bersama 2021) — OJK now requires larger KSPs to report financial data and comply with minimum liquidity ratios. For existing KSPs, this adds compliance burden.
64921.baliContext:
**🤝 The Indonesian Cooperative Landscape (Context for Foreign Investors)**

**Why this code matters to understand even if you can't use it:**
- Indonesia has 130,000+ registered cooperatives, of which ~20,000 are KSP; they collectively serve ~28 million member-borrowers
- KSP serves the UMKM segment that commercial banks won't touch: small traders, artisans, farmers, fishermen, temple offering sellers
- In Bali, the traditional Lembaga Perkreditan Desa (LPD) — Bali's unique village-level financial institution — operates alongside KSP serving the same base (LPD is actually NOT covered by KBLI 64921 — it has its own Perda Bali framework)
- The KSP sector in Indonesia has a troubled regulatory track record: several large KSPs (Indosurya IDR 15T, Sejahtera Bersama) collapsed under fraudulent management, wiping out millions of member savings

**The opportunity this points to for PMA investors:**
The gap that KSP serves — small loans (IDR 1–50 juta) for UMKM that commercial banks won't serve — is precisely where fintech P2P lending (66191) is growing fastest. If you want to serve Bali's 500,000+ UMKM operators (warungs, craftsmen, villa support businesses), P2P lending under 66191 is the legal PMA path.

**Bali LPD note:** The Lembaga Perkreditan Desa is a village-level financial institution unique to Bali, governed by Perda Bali No. 3/2017 — it is NOT a koperasi and NOT governed by KBLI 64921. Foreign investment in LPDs is similarly not permitted.

- **64992** — Multifinance/Perusahaan Pembiayaan (PMA alternative with vehicle leasing + working capital)
- **64194** — BPR Rural Bank (PMA alternative with max 40% foreign, OJK-licensed banking)
- **OJK legal counsel** — any financial services activity in Indonesia requires specialized regulatory legal advice; Kepmen 228/2019 and OJK regulations change frequently

64992.whatItMeans: Perusahaan Pembiayaan (multifinance company) — a non-bank financial institution that provides financing for: vehicle purchases (motor credit, car leasing), consumer goods, working capital for SMEs, property down payments, and factoring/receivables purchasing. Unlike a bank, a multifinance company cannot accept public deposits — it funds its portfolio from equity capital and bond issuance. Unlike P2P lending, it uses its own capital to extend credit (not matching borrowers with lenders). **Maximum foreign ownership: 85%** under OJK regulation (15% must be Indonesian). OJK governs under POJK 35/2018 (Penyelenggaraan Usaha Perusahaan Pembiayaan).
64992.whatYouNeed:
**Risk: Menengah Tinggi.** Authority: **Menteri** (OSS). OSS timeline 7 working days — but the OJK multifinance license is the critical gate (6–12 months).

**TWO-PHASE licensing — both mandatory:**

**PHASE 1 — OSS / NIB (7 working days):**
- Register PT PMA on OSS, select 64992, Menengah Tinggi
- NIB + Sertifikat Standar issued
- **Cannot extend financing to any customer without OJK license**

**PHASE 2 — OJK Multifinance License (POJK 35/2018) — 6–12 months:**
1. **Application to OJK** — Departemen Pengawasan IKNB I
2. **Minimum paid-up capital: IDR 100 miliar** — fully paid up at time of OJK application; largest minimum capital requirement in this session's codes
3. **Shareholders fit & proper test** — OJK vets all shareholders owning ≥ 25% and all directors/commissioners
4. **Business plan** — 5-year financial projections; portfolio composition (pembiayaan investasi, modal kerja, multiguna — each requires separate OJK approval of activities)
5. **IT infrastructure assessment** — OJK reviews loan origination system, credit scoring methodology, collections system
6. **Capital adequacy ratio:** OJK minimum gearing ratio (ratio modal terhadap pembiayaan) — typically multifinance must maintain minimum capital adequacy per POJK 35/2018
7. **OJK Izin Usaha** — issued after all stages pass
8. **Product-specific approvals** — each financing activity type (vehicle, property, multiguna) requires separate OJK product registration

**Step-by-step for PT PMA multifinance:**
1. **Establish PT PMA** — 85% foreign max, 15% Indonesian; notary deed, AHU (~4–6 weeks)
2. **Capital injection** — IDR 100 miliar fully paid up into Indonesian bank account (note: this is 4x larger than P2P lending requirement)
3. **NIB via OSS** — 64992, 7 working days
4. **OJK license application** — full dossier submission including business plan, credit policy, risk management framework, collections policy, IT system documentation
5. **OJK review and assessment** — includes site visit to office, interview with directors
6. **OJK Izin Usaha** — issued (~6–12 months from application)
7. **First financing transaction** — can commence immediately after Izin Usaha
8. **OJK ongoing reporting** — monthly financial reports; quarterly asset quality reports; annual audited financial statements

**Permitted financing activities (must be specified in OJK application):**
- **Pembiayaan Investasi** — productive assets: vehicle purchase (motor/mobil), machinery, equipment
- **Pembiayaan Modal Kerja** — working capital loans for SMEs
- **Pembiayaan Multiguna** — multi-purpose consumer financing
- **Sewa Pembiayaan (Finance Lease)** — asset leasing with option to purchase
- **Anjak Piutang (Factoring)** — purchasing receivables from vendors/sellers
- **KPA Bridging** — property down-payment financing (Kredit Pemilikan Apartemen bridging)

**Minimum total capital:** IDR 100 miliar paid-up — the highest capital requirement in this session.
**Maximum foreign ownership:** 85% (OJK POJK 35/2018); 15% Indonesian mandatory.
64992.whatChanged: Direct match from KBLI 2020 (MATCH_LANGSUNG). Key regulatory development: **OJK POJK 35/2018** (replacing POJK 29/2014) tightened capital adequacy requirements, added stronger consumer protection provisions, and introduced the distinction between pembiayaan investasi, modal kerja, and multiguna. Post-2022, OJK has increased scrutiny of multifinance NPL ratios following elevated defaults in motorcycle financing. OJK also imposed tighter debt-to-equity gearing limits (Net Gearing Ratio maximum 10x paid-up capital).
64992.baliContext:
**🚗 Multifinance in Bali — The Vehicle and Tourism Financing Market**

**The macro opportunity:**
- Indonesia's multifinance market: IDR 400+ triliun in receivables annually; dominated by Adira Finance (Astra group), BFI Finance, Mandiri Tunas Finance (bank-backed)
- Vehicle financing is the dominant product: Indonesia buys 6+ million motorcycles/year; Bali's tourism economy requires constant fleet renewal for motorbike rental companies, villa transport services, and tour operators

**The Bali-specific niches for a boutique PMA multifinance:**
- **Tourism fleet leasing:** Hotel and resort vehicle fleets (transport vans, minibuses, shuttle services) need finance lease arrangements; the asset is the collateral, appealing for Indonesian SME operators who lack land collateral for bank loans
- **Villa developer bridging:** Small villa developers (IDR 2–8B projects) need equity bridge financing for 12–24 months between construction start and villa sale; banks don't serve this size; P2P doesn't provide the right structure; a multifinance pembiayaan investasi product fills the gap
- **UMKM working capital — hospitality supply chain:** Restaurants, souvenir producers, food vendors need working capital advance against purchase orders from resorts; factoring/anjak piutang is the ideal product
- **Motorbike leasing for villa staff:** Villa and hotel staff who need motorbike transportation but can't qualify for bank consumer loans — high volume, small ticket, standardized credit scoring

**The IDR 100B capital reality:**
- IDR 100 miliar is ~USD 6.5 million — a meaningful commitment
- This filters out undercapitalized entrants and signals genuine intent to OJK
- For a 10x gearing ratio (max), IDR 100B capital supports IDR 1 triliun in financing portfolio — a significant operation

**⚠ Critical Issues**
- **NPL management is the business** — multifinance profitability depends entirely on credit quality; Bali's tourism economy is seasonal (NPL spikes in low season Oct–Mar as borrowers' cash flow weakens); build seasonal cash flow into credit underwriting
- **Gearing ratio ceiling** — maximum Net Gearing Ratio of 10x means your financing portfolio is capped at IDR 1T for IDR 100B capital; scaling beyond requires additional capital injection or bond issuance
- **Collections in Bali** — Indonesia's collections culture for consumer finance requires physical presence; motorbike repossession requires Fidusia (fiduciary lien registration at KEMENKUMHAM) before any collateral can be repossessed legally; skip this step and you lose all collateral rights

65121.whatItMeans: General insurance (non-life insurance) — providing insurance coverage for property, motor vehicles, marine cargo, fire, liability, health (group), travel, and other short-term risks. This covers all conventional non-life insurance products: car insurance, property insurance for villas/hotels, marine cargo insurance for shipments, travel insurance for tourists, group health insurance for companies. Policies are typically annual contracts renewed yearly. This is NOT life insurance (65111) or syariah insurance (65211) — this is conventional general insurance.
65121.whatYouNeed:
**BPS_ONLY code** — no `per_skala` data in KBLI 2025 JSON. The OSS licensing pathway shows: Risk: Tinggi (High). Authority: **Menteri/Kepala Badan** (ministerial level). Kewajiban: **Berbentuk badan hukum** (must be legal entity).

**Critical: NIB is NOT the insurance license**
The NIB from OSS is only the legal business entity registration. The actual insurance operating license comes from **OJK** (Otoritas Jasa Keuangan / Financial Services Authority) under **UU 40/2014** (Perasuransian / Insurance Law).

**Two-stage licensing process:**

**Stage 1: PT PMA Establishment + NIB**
1. **PT PMA incorporation** — notary deed, AHU registration; minimum IDR 10B stated capital (~3–5 weeks)
2. **NIB via OSS** — register on oss.go.id, select 65121, Tinggi path; NIB issued (~2–3 days)
3. **Kewajiban compliance** — "Berbentuk badan hukum" satisfied by PT PMA structure

**Stage 2: OJK Insurance License (Izin Usaha Perasuransian)**
4. **OJK application** — submit to OJK for Izin Usaha as general insurer
5. **Modal disetor minimum** — **IDR 100 billion** paid-up capital for new general insurance company (POJK requirement, far higher than PT PMA minimum)
6. **Fit & proper test** — all directors, commissioners, and controlling shareholders must pass OJK fit & proper assessment
7. **Business plan submission** — detailed actuarial projections, reinsurance arrangements, risk management framework
8. **Reinsurance treaty** — must have reinsurance agreements in place before OJK approval
9. **OJK approval timeline** — **6–18 months** from application to license issuance (highly variable depending on completeness)

**Post-license obligations:**
- Quarterly financial reporting to OJK
- Solvency margin compliance (Risk-Based Capital / RBC minimum 120%)
- Annual actuarial review and audit
- Consumer protection compliance (POJK 1/2013)

**Typical total timeline:** 12–24 months from PT PMA to operational insurance company (OJK license is the bottleneck).
**Minimum capital:** IDR 100 billion paid-up (OJK requirement) + IDR 10B PT PMA stated capital.

**Authority:** Menteri/Kepala Badan (OSS) + OJK (insurance license).
**PMA:** Historically 80% cap on foreign ownership for **acquisitions** of existing insurers. For **new establishment**, check current Perpres — PMA percentage may be limited. Verify with OJK before proceeding.
65121.whatChanged: General insurance existed in KBLI 2020 under similar codes. KBLI 2025 maintains the classification as BPS_ONLY, meaning detailed per-scale licensing data is not yet fully defined in OSS. The core regulatory framework remains OJK-based under UU 40/2014, unchanged from previous years.
65121.baliContext:
**🏝 General Insurance in Bali (Active Market, High Barriers to Entry)**
- Bali has significant demand for general insurance: property insurance for villas/hotels (fire, earthquake, flood), motor vehicle insurance (massive market — millions of vehicles), marine cargo insurance (Benoa port shipments), travel insurance for tourists
- **Existing players dominate:** Major Indonesian insurers (Asuransi Astra, Sinar Mas, Allianz Indonesia, ACA, Zurich) already have strong distribution in Bali
- **Expat market:** International health insurance plans (CIGNA, AIA, Allianz) serve expat community; group health insurance for companies is a growing segment

---

**💡 PMA Opportunities (Realistic Assessment)**
- **Establishing a new general insurer is extremely difficult:** IDR 100B capital requirement, 12–24 month OJK approval process, intense competition from established players
- **More practical path: Insurance agency (66221)** — act as intermediary selling insurance products on behalf of existing insurers; much lower capital requirement (IDR 10B PT PMA only), faster licensing, immediate revenue
- **Niche opportunities:** Specialty insurance for tourism sector (villa rental insurance, tour operator liability, event cancellation), marine insurance for yacht/boat owners, expat health insurance brokerage
- **Acquisition route:** Buying an existing small general insurer may be faster than new establishment, but PMA cap (historically 80% for acquisitions) applies — verify current regulations

---

**⚠ Critical Points for Foreign Investors**
- **OJK license is separate and mandatory:** Do not assume NIB = permission to operate insurance business; OJK Izin Usaha is the critical license
- **IDR 100B capital is real:** This is paid-up capital, not stated capital; you must actually deposit IDR 100 billion into the company bank account
- **Fit & proper test is strict:** OJK will reject directors/commissioners with poor financial history, criminal records, or insufficient insurance industry experience
- **Reinsurance is mandatory:** General insurers must have reinsurance treaties to manage risk; this requires relationships with international reinsurers
- **Consider agency model first:** 66221 (insurance agent) is a much more accessible entry point into Bali's insurance market — test the market before committing IDR 100B to a new insurer

- **74100** — Business consulting — if you provide risk management consulting alongside insurance products

66125.whatItMeans: Money changer (foreign exchange services) — buying and selling foreign currencies and traveler's cheques at physical exchange counters. This is the classic money changer business model: tourists and locals exchange USD, EUR, AUD, SGD, JPY, CNY for Indonesian Rupiah (and vice versa). Physical counter operations, not digital/fintech forex trading. This code covers authorized money changing activity regulated by Bank Indonesia, distinct from unauthorized/illegal money changers.
66125.whatYouNeed:
**Risk: Tinggi (High). Authority: Menteri/Kepala Badan. Timeline: Otomatis (NIB auto-issued). Kewajiban: Berbentuk badan hukum.**

**Critical: This is Bank Indonesia (BI) regulated, NOT OJK**
Money changing falls under **Bank Indonesia** jurisdiction, not OJK. The regulatory framework is **PBI 18/20/PBI/2016** (Kegiatan Usaha Penukaran Valuta Asing Bukan Bank / KUPVA-BB).

**Two-stage licensing process:**

**Stage 1: PT PMA Establishment + NIB**
1. **PT PMA incorporation** — notary deed, AHU registration; minimum IDR 10B stated capital (~3–5 weeks)
2. **NIB via OSS** — register on oss.go.id, select 66125, Tinggi path; NIB auto-issued (Otomatis) (~2–3 days)
3. **Kewajiban compliance** — "Berbentuk badan hukum" satisfied by PT PMA structure

**Stage 2: Bank Indonesia KUPVA-BB License**
4. **BI application** — submit to Bank Indonesia for KUPVA-BB (Kegiatan Usaha Penukaran Valuta Asing Bukan Bank) license
5. **Modal disetor minimum** — **IDR 500 million** paid-up capital (much lower than OJK financial products)
6. **Location requirements** — physical office/counter in commercial area, tourism zone, or airport; BI inspects premises before approval
7. **KYC/AML systems** — must have Know Your Customer and Anti-Money Laundering procedures in place (BI regulation)
8. **Exchange rate transparency** — must display BI-approved exchange rates prominently; rate manipulation is prohibited
9. **BI approval timeline** — **2–6 months** from application to license issuance

**Post-license obligations:**
- Display BI license prominently at counter (mandatory)
- Daily transaction reporting to BI for transactions > IDR 100 million
- KYC documentation for large transactions (passport copy, transaction purpose)
- Exchange rate posting (buy/sell rates must be visible to customers)
- Annual audit and BI inspection compliance

**Typical total timeline:** 3–8 months from PT PMA to operational money changer (BI license + premises setup).
**Minimum capital:** IDR 500 million paid-up (BI requirement) + IDR 10B PT PMA stated capital.

**Authority:** Menteri/Kepala Badan (OSS) + Bank Indonesia (KUPVA-BB license).
**PMA:** Fully open (Terbuka) — 100% foreign ownership.
66125.whatChanged: Renumbered in KBLI 2025 (CODICE_RINUMERATO). Money changing existed under a different code in KBLI 2020. The regulatory framework under Bank Indonesia (PBI 18/20/PBI/2016) remains unchanged — same licensing requirements, same BI oversight.
66125.baliContext:
**💱 Money Changers in Bali (Massive Market, Scam Problem)**
- Bali has hundreds of money changers: Seminyak, Kuta, Ubud, Sanur, airports, shopping malls — everywhere tourists go
- **Tourist volume drives demand:** Millions of foreign arrivals annually exchanging currency; still high cash usage in Bali despite digital payments
- **Scam epidemic:** Illegal/unlicensed money changers use unfair practices (short-changing, fake notes, rigged calculators, hidden fees); tourists regularly get scammed
- **Licensed vs. unlicensed:** BI-licensed money changers display license prominently; unlicensed operators do not

---

**💡 PMA Opportunities in This Sector**
- **Premium legal money changer:** Transparent rates, BI-licensed, professional service — differentiate from scam operators by being visibly legitimate
- **Strategic locations:** Airport (Ngurah Rai), Seminyak (Jl. Raya Seminyak, Jl. Kayu Aya), Ubud (Jl. Raya Ubud), Sanur (Jl. Danau Tamblingan) — high tourist foot traffic
- **Multi-location chain:** Establish 3–5 counters across Bali's main tourist areas; economies of scale on compliance and branding
- **Hotel partnerships:** In-house money changing service for 4–5 star hotels (commission-sharing model)
- **Competitive advantage:** BI license = trust; many tourists actively seek licensed changers after scam experiences

---

**⚠ Critical Points for Money Changer Operators**
- **BI license is mandatory:** Operating without KUPVA-BB license = illegal; BI conducts raids and imposes fines; criminal penalties possible
- **Display BI license prominently:** Customers must be able to see your BI license number and validity; this is your competitive advantage over illegal operators
- **KYC compliance is strict:** Large transactions (> IDR 100M) require customer identification; failure to comply = BI sanctions
- **Exchange rate transparency:** Buy/sell rates must be clearly posted; rate manipulation or hidden fees = BI violation
- **Cash security:** Money changers are robbery targets; invest in proper security (safe, CCTV, security guard for high-volume locations)
- **Competition is intense:** Hundreds of money changers in Bali; differentiate through location, service quality, and visible legitimacy (BI license)
